title: Biological nitrogen fixation for non-legumes
bottleneck: Legumes fix their own nitrogen via symbiosis, but cereals — which feed most of humanity — cannot, forcing dependence on synthetic fertilizer. Engineering nitrogen fixation into cereals means either transferring the 20-gene nitrogenase pathway, which is poisoned by oxygen and enormously energy-expensive, or building synthetic symbiosis with diazotrophs; both have defeated decades of effort. The biochemistry fights the plant at every step. Nitrogenase is poisoned by oxygen and enormously energy-expensive, so the plant must be re-engineered around it.
why_it_blocks: Self-fertilizing cereals would eliminate the Haber-Bosch dependence that defines modern agriculture's energy and pollution footprint. Self-fertilizing cereals would erase the Haber-Bosch dependence that defines modern agriculture's footprint.
current_state: Research groups report nitrogen-fixing bacterial associations with modest effects; true engineered fixation in cereals remains a distant goal.
